flashcard_questions.q: What does fard mean in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: A compulsory religious duty for every adult Muslim of sound mind.

flashcard_questions.q: Which pillar requires fasting during the month of Ramadan?
Which pillar requires pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in a lifetime?
What percentage of savings must a Muslim give as Zakah?
How many daily prayers does Salah require?
Which extra duty requires Shi’a Muslims to pay 20% of surplus income?
Which pillar is missing from the Shi’a Ten Obligatory Acts?
What does the first half of the Shahadah affirm?
What does the second half of the Shahadah acknowledge?
flashcard_questions.a: That Muhammad is God’s final messenger.

flashcard_questions.q: What third clause do Shi’a Muslims add to the Shahadah?
flashcard_questions.a: “And Ali is the friend of God”.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do Shi’a Muslims add Ali to the declaration of faith?
flashcard_questions.a: They believe Ali was divinely appointed as Muhammad’s successor.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the only requirement for converting to Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: Sincerely reciting the Shahadah before Muslim witnesses.

flashcard_questions.q: When is the Shahadah first spoken to a Muslim baby?
flashcard_questions.a: It is whispered into the newborn’s ear.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the Shahadah placed first among the Five Pillars?
flashcard_questions.a: Without belief in one God and Muhammad’s prophethood, the other pillars have no meaning.

notes: 14 cards: 4 practice→pillar (Sawm, Hajj, Zakah rate, Salah frequency), 4 term→definition (fard, Khums, Tawhid clause, conversion requirement), 3 denomination→position (Shi’a third clause, missing Shahadah, Ali’s succession), 2 practice→meaning (newborn, why first), 1 attribution. Left the Five Pillars list itself off the deck — it only works as an enumeration.
